<description>
This is split off from #36521 (and not included in #36895), as it's effectively an independent improvement.

This introduces a number of additional checks that are applied during transaction deserialization, which reduce various worst case deserialization time scenarios:
* Reject transactions with more txins or more txouts than can possibly fit in a block (applied always)
* Reject transactions with 0 txins or 0 txouts (applied in P2P code only; there are RPCs like `fundrawtransaction` that explicitly support transactions with 0 inputs)
* Count weight accurately during transaction or block deserialization, and bail out as soon as it exceeds 4M (applied in P2P code).

This is a mild behavior change, as detecting these problems early causes them to be treated as deserialization errors, which in P2P logic cause messages to be ignored instead of peer disconnection.
</description>

<commits>
039f5ce69d primitives: reject txs with more inputs or outputs than fit in a block

When deserializing a transaction, read the input and output counts
first, and fail before reading the inputs or outputs if more of them
are claimed than can fit in a block, given their minimum size (41 bytes
for an input, 9 for an output). Such a transaction can never be valid.

This allows us to allocate the vin and vout vectors immediately, rather
than sequentially in batches of 5 MB as the std::vector deserializer
does, because that memory becomes bounded: to 2.7 MB for 24390 inputs,
and 5.3 MB for 111111 outputs. It is a preparation for further changes
that rely on this structuring of conditionals.

This affects all places where transactions are deserialized. Through
RPC, such transactions can no longer be decoded. From P2P, a transaction
or block containing one is ignored like other malformed messages, rather
than rejected by validation.

9de186b527 p2p: reject transactions without inputs or outputs when deserializing

Add a reject_empty flag to TransactionSerParams, which makes
deserialization fail as soon as a transaction is found to have no
inputs or no outputs. Such transactions are never valid, but are
currently fully deserialized (along with the rest of the message) before
validation rejects them.

This reduces the memory a peer can make us allocate by sending a block
full of such transactions. At 10 bytes each, about 400000 of them fit in
a block message, each of which gets its own CTransaction. With this
change, the smallest transaction that gets deserialized has one input
and one output, which takes 60 bytes.

The flag is enabled (as TX_WITH_WITNESS_P2P) only where transactions are
received from P2P peers: tx and block messages, and the transactions in
cmpctblock and blocktxn messages. Like other malformed messages, these
are now ignored, rather than, for a block, causing the peer to be
disconnected, or, for a transaction, being added to the reject filters.
The functional tests are updated accordingly.

a0356ec949 refactor: use the stream's parameters for compact block transactions

BlockTransactions and PrefilledTransaction (de)serialized their
transactions with TX_WITH_WITNESS_P2P, overriding any parameters of the
stream. Use the stream's parameters instead, like CBlock does, and pass
TX_WITH_WITNESS where they are serialized and TX_WITH_WITNESS_P2P where
data from peers is deserialized. This does not change behavior
(serialization only depends on allow_witness), but makes it possible to
deserialize them with other parameters. Tests that are not about data
from peers do so, with TX_WITH_WITNESS.

4e3e542a6c serialize: add StreamHasParams concept

Constrain ParamsStream::GetParams() to the parameter types that the
stream, or a stream it wraps, has. Before, calling it for another type
failed inside the function body, which cannot be tested for.

With that, add a StreamHasParams<Stream, P> concept, which tells whether
GetParams() can be called on a stream of type Stream.

This does not change what compiles. Calling GetParams() for a type
the stream does not have is now reported as an unsatisfied constraint
at the call site.

b277e34b1a serialize: add support for caller-owned state when (de)serializing

Add WithState<State>, serialization parameters that hold a reference to
state: a mutable object owned by the caller. They are used like other
parameters: WithState{state}(obj) (de)serializes obj through a stream
that has them. The code that (de)serializes obj, and everything inside
it, can look the object up by its type using GetSerState<State>(s).
That only compiles for streams that have such state; the
StreamHasState<Stream, State> concept tells whether a stream does, for
code for which the state is optional.

This makes it possible to keep track of something across everything
that is (de)serialized, for example to limit the total size of what is
deserialized, while the parameters of the types that are (de)serialized
stay plain values. As the state is an object in the caller, its
lifetime is explicit there, and the same object can be used for several
objects that are (de)serialized separately.

A stream should refer to only one object of each state type. So let
parameter types declare that they cannot be overridden, with a
NO_OVERRIDE member, as WithState does: creating a ParamsStream with
such parameters for a stream that already has them is a compile-time
error.

As these are ordinary parameters, they can be combined with other ones
in any order, they do not depend on which streams get created or copied
along the way, and they stay available to code that is (de)serialized
with parameters of its own.

aaea704057 p2p: limit the weight of transactions and blocks while deserializing

Add TxWeightBudget, a limit on the total weight of deserialized
transactions. The code that deserializes creates one, and applies it to
what it deserializes using WithState. The budget is then decremented
while transactions are being deserialized (charging the minimum weight
of inputs and outputs before allocating memory for them), causing
failure as soon as the budget is exceeded.

Use this for tx, block, cmpctblock and blocktxn messages, with a budget
of MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT minus the header: the transactions in a block,
cmpctblock or blocktxn message are part of one block (for blocktxn, this
does not account for those of the block that are already known), and a
transaction that does not fit in a block cannot be valid.

To make sure that the budget is not left out where data from peers is
deserialized, give TX_WITH_WITNESS_P2P a type of its own,
P2PTransactionSerParams, which derives from TransactionSerParams. The
type acts as a compile-time parameter, stating that the weight of what
is deserialized is limited: deserializing transactions through a stream
that has these parameters, but no TxWeightBudget, does not compile. The
requirement only exists as long as the parameters keep their type: code
that receives them as a TransactionSerParams can still deserialize with
them without a budget.

The P2P message size limit allows blocks of up to 4 MB, which is up to
16M weight, all of which is currently deserialized before validation
rejects it (unless a transaction has more inputs or outputs than fit in
a block). With this change, the weight deserialized from a message is
at most MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT minus the header.

Messages exceeding the budget are ignored, like other malformed
messages, rather than causing the peer to be disconnected for sending an
invalid block.
